div.head: Wi 27[b]
div.ab: gif hine man acwelle, þam agende hi man healfne agelde.
gif hine man acwelle, þam agende hine man healfne agelde.
Gif hine man acwelle, þam agende hi[ne] man healfne agelde.
wenn man jenen [Dieb] tödtet, entgelte man ihn dem Inhaber zur Hälfte.
if that [thief] is killed, let him be paid for to his owner at half.
If he is put to death, half his value shall be paid to the man who has him in his power.
If he [the slave] is put to death, one should pay the owner half his [the slave’s] value.

note.seg: Das Gericht, nachdem der König die Begnadigung ablehnte
The court, after the king had refused pardon
Der Zahlende ist der Herr; denn der Sklave hat weder Sippe noch 70 Schilling, über diese s. Gl unfrei 7
The one who pays is the lord; for the slave has neither kindred nor 70 shillings; on the latter see Gl unfrei 7

Einfänger, regelmässig mit bestohlenem Kläger identisch; vgl. o. 26, 1². Den Eigentümer des Sklaven verstanden Frühere gemäss Hl 1. Aber dieser kann doch nicht vom Gericht auf Staatskosten oder vom Kläger dáfür bezahlt werden, dass er ein gemeinschädliches Wertstück nicht gehörig bewacht hat. Auch Hl 1. 3 lässt ihn neben dessen Auslieferung büssen

The captor, as a rule identical with the robbed plaintiff; cf. above 26, 1². Earlier editors understood the owner of the slave, in accordance with Hl 1. But he can surely not be paid by the court at public expense, or by the plaintiff, for having failed to guard properly a valuable piece of property that was a danger to the community. Hl 1. 3, too, makes him pay compensation in addition to handing the slave over

note.label: hine
note.note: The number 1 is printed 2 times on the page (27[a], 27[b]), with one footnote.

note.seg: The word properly means ‘owner’; but, as Liebermann points out, the context here requires that the man who possesses his person at the moment must be meant.

note.label: owner
note.seg: It is not clear what ‘the owner’ refers to here. It seems unlikely that it is the owner of the slave (who should have overseen his property better). Liebermann and Attenborough both assume that it is the man who currently holds the slave in his power. But I think it most likely that the payment goes to the man whose property was stolen.
